tier_reason: Code (matrix_benchmark.c, matrix_benchmark_gas.s, Makefile), GCC 12.2.0 and flags are public but no CPU model is given, so at most C; the comparison itself is ISA-unequal (hand-written AVX2/FMA against a C build with CFLAGS = -O3 -Wall -Wextra -fPIE and no -march/-mavx2/-mfma, so GCC can only emit baseline x86-64 SSE2 code), which follows the AssemblyScript precedent for a baseline crippled by a build default (C to D).

corrections.caveats: Baseline crippled by build flags: the Makefile builds the C benchmark with -O3 -Wall -Wextra -fPIE only, so GCC 12.2.0 targets baseline x86-64 (SSE2, 2-wide, no FMA) while the assembly uses 256-bit AVX2 vfmadd231pd; the 1.66x mostly measures vector width and FMA, not hand-written code, and an -O3 -march=x86-64-v3 (or -mavx2 -mfma) build of the same i-k-j loop was never measured. The README's statement that gcc -O3 'auto-vectorizes with AVX' and emits vmulpd + vaddpd cannot be true for the stated flags. The asm binary has no CPU dispatch and needs AVX2/FMA. The repo description says 'Assembly is ~150% faster' while the README data show 1.66x (66% faster). CPU model not stated; five runs of one 200x200 size; single-author toy project (4 commits on 2026-05-12, 0 stars). Outputs differ by up to 1.42e-14 (FMA single rounding); the asm does zero C and run 1,000 full multiplications, so the timing is not a no-op.

notes: Numbers on the README match the record (C 3.043 s vs asm 1.823 s mean internal timer, 1.66x, about 2.63 vs 4.39 GFLOP/s). Main shortcoming: the C baseline was built without -mavx2/-mfma, so it cannot use the instructions the asm uses; no fair compiler comparison exists. MIT licence, last commit 2026-05-12, metadata otherwise correct.

tier_reason: First-party cycle-count table; the harness is public (test/prepare_csv_benchmarks.c with the REPORT_BENCHMARK_CSV macro in test/report.inc, raw data in docs/esp_bm_results.csv, table built by docs/build_bm_table.py) and the chips are named, but the compiler name and version are not stated, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Page values (CPU cycles, -O2): ESP32-S3 asm vs the table's 'ANSI Xtensa' column: dsps_dotprod_f32 N=256 432 vs 1311 (3.0x), dsps_dotprod_s16 307 vs 3635 (11.8x), dsps_fft2r_sc16 1024 points 15,623 vs 221,955 (14.2x), dsps_fir_f32 1024 samples/256 coeffs 443,671 vs 1,353,122 (3.0x), dsps_fft2r_fc32 1024 points 97,847 vs 175,729 (1.8x) (all derived from page data). The 'ANSI Xtensa' column holds the ESP32's ANSI values (build_bm_table.py writes ESP32 and ESP32-S3 ANSI results into the same column and the ESP32 rows come last in docs/esp_bm_results.csv); the S3's own same-chip ANSI values in that CSV give dotprod_f32 432 vs 1311 (3.0x), dotprod_s16 307 vs 2864 (9.3x), fft2r_sc16 1024 15,623 vs 214,764 (13.7x), fir_f32 443,671 vs 1,350,660 (3.0x), fft2r_fc32 1024 97,847 vs 174,698 (1.8x) (derived from page data). ESP32-P4 dsps_dotprod_s16 208 vs 3385 ANSI Risc-V (16.3x, derived). Rows with no gain or a loss: ESP32 dsps_fir_f32 1,078,691 vs 1,353,122 (1.25x), ESP32-P4 dsps_fir_f32 1,606,563 vs 1,606,552 (parity), ESP32 dsps_fft2r_sc16 1024 points 226,154 vs 221,955 (asm slower), ESP32-P4 dspm_mult_3x3x3_f32 338 vs 309 and dspm_mult_4x4x4_f32 658 vs 608 (asm slower at -O2), ESP32 dspi_dotprod image rows equal to ANSI (no ESP32 asm path).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: ESP-IDF compiler optimization settings: CONFIG_COMPILER_OPTIMIZATION_PERF (the 'O2' columns) and CONFIG_COMPILER_OPTIMIZATION_SIZE (the 'Os' columns); compiler name and version not stated (ESP-IDF GCC toolchain assumed).
corrections.caveats: First-party table; compiler name and version not stated. Harness (test/prepare_csv_benchmarks.c, REPORT_BENCHMARK_CSV in test/report.inc) makes one warm-up call, then times a single call with interrupts masked using the CPU cycle counter, so each value is one sample; the page itself points to test/test_dsp.c. The 'ANSI Xtensa' column is the ESP32's ANSI run, so ESP32-S3 ratios against it are cross-chip; the S3's own ANSI numbers are in docs/esp_bm_results.csv and give slightly lower ratios (dotprod_s16 9.3x instead of 11.8x). Several rows show no gain or a loss (ESP32 fft2r_sc16, ESP32-P4 fir_f32, ESP32-P4 3x3x3 and 4x4x4 matrix multiply, ESP32 image dot products). The README says many functions are written in assembly; ANSI C reference implementations are the baseline, not an outside library.

notes: All claimed numbers appear on the benchmarks page and the ratios check out, but the 'ANSI Xtensa' baseline column is the ESP32's ANSI run (build_bm_table.py overwrites the S3 value), so S3 ratios are cross-chip; same-chip ratios from docs/esp_bm_results.csv were added. Apache-2.0, 715 stars, last commit 2026-05-11 confirmed.

tier_reason: First-party README tick counts; per-kernel harness code is public (tests/src/*_test.c time the ANSI and optimized kernel with profile_c_start/profile_opt_start and check outputs equal) and flags are in CMakeLists.txt, with chip and clock stated, but the compiler version is not given, so not A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: -O2 -Wno-unused-function for the component (ESP32-S3 adds -mlongcalls -fno-unroll-loops), from CMakeLists.txt; compiler name and version not stated (ESP-IDF GCC toolchain assumed).
corrections.caveats: First-party table of tick (CPU cycle) counts; compiler version not stated. Harness: tests/src/*_test.c call the ANSI and optimized kernel once each around profile_c_start/profile_opt_start and CHECK_EQUAL the outputs, so the optimized kernels must match the reference bit-exactly; single samples. Kernel tables were last refreshed in April 2026 (S3 and P4; fully connected Aug 2026, S31 Aug 2026) and predate the Sep 2026 S3 conv/FC/softmax perf work and the Oct 7-8 2026 correctness fixes (e102c97 S3 max pool activation_min when channels % 8 == 4; 8303c3b and 538d722 P4 PIE unaligned stores and access bits, which touch max pool); the P4 max pool 19.94x was measured before its unaligned-store fix (the S3 max pool test shape has 16 channels and is outside the %8==4 bug). ESP32-S3 kernels are largely hand-written .S files; P4/S31 kernels are mostly C with inline PIE assembly. Rows mix external (PSRAM) and internal memory placement. Model-level timings (Person Detection S3 2300 ms vs 54 ms, MobileNetV3, YOLO11n) compare TFLite Micro with and without ESP-NN, not asm against the same C.

notes: All claimed numbers match the README tables (S3 conv 14.24x, prelu 11.48x, max pool 7.83x, fully connected 5.47x, softmax 1.37x; P4 max pool 19.94x, conv 7.00x, hard_swish 1.36x). Shortcomings: compiler version unstated, single-sample timings, tables predate October 2026 max-pool correctness fixes. Apache-2.0, 274 stars, last commit 2026-10-08 confirmed.
